terminal_basis.derivation: derived by issue35_envelope.derive_terminal from the effective classifications and marginal facts (UTILITY-ENVELOPE.json schema /3 carries the machine derivation); validate_terminal enforces consistency fail-closed
terminal_basis.note: Re-derived strictly from the Issue #35 terminal definitions and the retained evidence. X1_PARTICIPANT_ONLY_CAPACITY_USEFUL is permitted only when the bounded tested roles establish real capacity utility but NO throughput-neutral/positive serving role under current supported semantics. The retained supported serving-role evidence contains x1p-role-adverse = THROUGHPUT_POSITIVE (55.95 vs the AMD single-subject 44.4 t/s, ratio 1.2601; peer-perspective ratio against the stronger NV anchor 0.622), so that terminal is not permitted by the issue's own definition. The measured envelope instead establishes the minimum viable participant envelope: it distinguishes at least (1) decisive capacity/residency utility on measured memory-fit facts (106.5x vs the pressured control); (2) conditional single-sequence throughput utility depending on anchor compute strength (1.2601x adding the stronger participant to the weaker anchor; 0.622x the reverse); (3) no demonstrated benefit for the corrected four-concurrent-request coarse role (first attempt decisively below the control, second attempt inside the neutral band, no attempt beyond the band, no separate capacity benefit); (4) unsupported finer row/tensor split on this substrate (fails closed, R0); and (5) device/backend compute rate as an explicit crossover input (device-local ratio 2.026 between subjects), rather than an x1/vendor special case. ENVELOPE_ESTABLISHED does not require every tested throughput role to be positive; that is not the terminal definition.
